requirements.title: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence concentration within Computer Science BA
One concentration elective
requirements.summary: Choose one listed option for the stated group units; blank individual course credits remain unverified.

requirements.title: Optional concentration and host-major overlap
requirements.summary: Concentrations allow majors to develop a level of depth in a particular area of computer science. Courses taken toward a concentration may also apply to the upper-division elective requirements of the major. Concentrations are optional, and so are not required by the computer science major. Participation in the cyber security concentration requires approval of the chair and the dean of the Shiley-Marcos School of Engineering.

requirements.title: Semester credit definition
requirements.summary: One undergraduate unit is credit for one hour of classroom work plus at least two outside-work hours each week over an approximately 14-week semester or equivalent. USD explicitly operates on a semester system; published amounts are normalized as semester hours.

requirements.title: Host-major declaration and program changes
requirements.summary: First-time first-year students may declare a major after April 15 of their first year. Declaration and changes follow the relevant college/school process; the school assigns a faculty advisor. This does not invent a separate AI-concentration form or deadline.

requirements.title: Host-degree residence context
requirements.summary: The final 30 semester units ordinarily must be completed at USD. A dean may partially waive this for valid educational reasons when most academic work was completed at USD. This is host-degree context, not 30 extra concentration units.

requirements.title: Host-major GPA and minimum-grade context
requirements.summary: Maintain at least 2.0 GPA at USD and in upper-division major courses. At least 24 upper-division units used for the major require C-minus or better; transferred courses count toward that 24-unit threshold only with C or better, subject to department limits. These are major-wide conditions, not a blanket C-minus assertion for every AI elective.

requirements.title: Computer Science residence and grading
requirements.summary: Both CS degrees require at least 15 upper-division units at USD; their own major pages specify upper-division major units. The school distinguishes this from the 24-unit engineering-program rule. Pass/fail is not permitted for courses required by prefix/title or for major-required electives.

requirements.title: Concurrent major/minor overlap context
requirements.summary: Upper-division courses may count toward multiple majors unless the department restricts this; interdisciplinary majors prohibit double-major course sharing. Minor courses cannot count toward the major, though they may satisfy preparation or core. The AI concentration’s own rule separately permits sharing with upper-division major electives.

requirements.title: Transfer approval and grades
requirements.summary: Transfer courses require at least C-minus and normally cannot be P/S/CR; the published exception covers Spring 2020–Summer 2021. Credits transfer without GPA points, on USD’s semester system (quarter hours ×2/3), without exceeding source credit. USD determines whether they satisfy the major; documentation and official transcripts are required.

requirements.title: Outside study after matriculation
requirements.summary: Up to 18 units may transfer after enrollment. A Transfer Class Petition needs advisor/university approval; major use also needs department/program review. Petition before enrolling to avoid rejection. Unaffiliated international courses need advance department, advisor and dean approval; affiliated study abroad is articulated. Repeated equivalent content ordinarily receives no credit unless the earlier USD course grade was D or F.

requirements.title: Transfer eligibility boundaries
requirements.summary: Accredited undergraduate work is considered, but life-experience, vocational, remedial, institution-introduction and most extension/continuing-education courses are excluded. Credit-by-exam is restricted to the published approved programs. Activity/athletics transfer is capped at four units per category. USD BPS/distance-completion credits apply only to those programs, not these in-person CS degrees.

requirements.title: No duplicate credit
requirements.summary: A course must add to prior learning: duplicate previous work and elementary prerequisites taken concurrently with or after advanced work do not earn additional degree credit.
